title: model-loading-breadcrumbs-scratchpad-sofia-alvarez
content:
Breadcrumbs: model loading failures (weights download / sharding / checkpoint format)

Summary:
- Observed intermittent model load failures on dedicated and private deployments when loading large LLM checkpoints (30–70GB). Failures happen during weights download or immediately after when validating shard manifests. Mostly reproducible on recovery after node restart and during scale-up.
- Symptoms: partial download, checksum mismatch, safetensors vs .pt format errors, occasional 502/504 from object store.

Incident timeline (rough):
- 2025-02-12 03:40 UTC: first noisy alert (model load failed) from Canary group (canary-model-xx).
- 2025-02-12 03:41 UTC: restart of worker node A triggered auto-recovery -> failure repeated.
- 2025-02-13 10:12 UTC: repeated during scale-up of Dedicated pool (burst), multiple hosts hit.
- 2025-02-14 09:00 UTC: started manual debug, collected logs.

Commands / experiments tried (raw):
- curl / aws / gsutil to fetch shard directly (to reproduce):
  - aws s3 cp s3://models-prod/llama-70b/checkpoint-000/pytorch_model-00001-of-00010.safetensors ./tmp/ || echo $?
  - gsutil -m cp gs://redwood-models/llama-70b/* ./tmp/ || echo $?
  - rclone copy remote:models/llama-70b tmp/ -P --retries 5
- md5/sha checks:
  - md5sum pytorch_model-00001-of-00010.safetensors && sha256sum pytorch_model-00001-of-00010.safetensors
- runtime debug: tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/runtime.log | grep -i "checkpoint"
- docker logs inference-runtime-xyz --since 1h | grep -i "shard"
- python repro script: python tools/repro_load.py --checkpoint s3://... --verbose
- tested with new downloader binary (v1.4.2) and older (v1.3.8) to rule out regression

Observed error snippets (copied verbatim):
- "ChecksumMismatchError: expected sha256=3f2a... but got 000000..."
- "Failed to open safetensors: invalid header (expected 'safetensors' magic)"
- "Exception: IncompleteRead(0 bytes read)" (from urllib3)
- "Error fetching shard: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout"
- Python stack: File \"/app/loader.py\", line 214, in _download_shard
    raise DownloadError(f'failed to download {shard.name}: {e}')
- Runtime log excerpt: "[2025-02-14T09:12:10Z] WARN shard-validate: manifest mismatch: shard index 4 missing in manifest for checkpoint-000"

Hypotheses / notes:
- transient object-store network issues (504/timeout) cause partial downloads, downstream checksum fails.
- for some uploads the manifest (checkpoint.json) does not list shards consistently (upload race or incomplete manifest write).
- safetensors vs torch .pt mix-up: older tool uploaded a .pt renamed to .safetensors (corrupt magic) -> loader fails on header. Could be a human or CI bug during model onboarding.
- aggressive S3 lifecycle / replication causing eventual consistency and HEAD requests returning before object is available in region (rare).
- downloader has insufficient retry/backoff and doesn't validate stream length before writing file -> partial file left behind gets validated and triggers checksum mismatch.
- checksum computed at upload time differs from download due to chunking/transfer encoding? less likely.

Repro attempts and outcomes:
- Reproduced partial download locally by simulating network drop (tc qdisc) -> download aborted with IncompleteRead, checksum mismatch appears.
- Reproduced invalid safetensors header by taking a small .pt file and renaming -> loader fails with same 'invalid header' error. So loader correctly detects format mismatch.
- Using rclone with --retries 10 + --buffer-size 256M reduced occurrence (suggests transient network).
- Running downloader v1.4.2 (contains streaming validation) fixed some cases (fewer partial files), but still saw one manifest-mismatch case.

Logs / relevant excerpts (sanitized):
- /var/log/redwood/runtime.log:
  [2025-02-14T09:11:58Z] INFO starting shard-download: checkpoint-000 shard=00003 size=512MB
  [2025-02-14T09:12:01Z] ERROR download-failed: checkpoint-000 shard=00003 err=HTTP 504
  [2025-02-14T09:12:10Z] WARN shard-validate: manifest mismatch: shard index 4 missing in manifest for checkpoint-000
  [2025-02-14T09:12:11Z] ERROR model-load: failed validating shards for checkpoint-000

- python repro output (snippet):
  Downloading shard 00003
  Opened stream -> read 0 bytes -> raising IncompleteRead
  Traceback (most recent calls):
    File "tools/repro_load.py", line 42, in <module>
      load_checkpoint(args.checkpoint)
    File "/app/loader.py", line 214, in load_checkpoint
      raise DownloadError(f'failed to download {shard}: {e}')

Immediate mitigations tried:
- Re-run model onboarding pipeline for affected model with checksum verification step (manual reupload of shards).
- Rolled back downloader to v1.3.8 on one host (no improvement).
- Increased downloader retries and added temporary backoff config (on dedicated only).
- For a customer private deployment, advised to resync model artifacts from central repo; customer performed re-sync and reported success.

Proposed root cause and remediation plan (current thinking):
1) Primary cause = transient network/object-store errors combined with downloader not being robust enough (missing atomic write + validate-before-rename). Partial files remain and validation fails in a way that leads to weird manifest messages.
2) Secondary cause = some malformed uploads (wrong extension/format) slipped through onboarding CI -> loader errors on format check.

Short-term (next 24–72h):
- Add robust atomic write + checksum validation in downloader: write to tmp file, verify size+sha256, then rename into final path (PR ready, see linked PR). (owner: Jordan)
- Increase default retries + exponential backoff in downloader config for Dedicated and Private deployments (ops change rollout). (owner: SRE)
- Add a small `post-upload verify` job in onboarding CI that re-downloads a sample byte-range and validates header+magic for safetensors/.pt to catch bad uploads. (owner: Maya)
- Manual resync of affected checkpoints and re-run model-load smoke tests (owner: Sofia)

Longer-term (weeks):
- Improve manifest/versioning guarantees: make manifest writes atomic (upload new manifest to manifest.tmp then mv) and include per-shard content-length + sha256 in manifest so loader can detect inconsistencies earlier. (proposal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-manifests/pull/12)
- Instrument runtime to emit per-shard download latency and byte counts to trace partial download patterns. Create alert when >N% downloads get 0 bytes or timeouts. (owner: observability)
- Harden onboarding CI to reject mismatched file-headers (safetensors magic mismatch).(owner: applied-ml onboarding)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Which uploads were performed by older tooling? Check onboarding pipeline logs for uploads between 2024-11 and 2025-01. (Action: Jordan to query S3 logs)
- Are there bucket lifecycle rules or replication lag between regions that could cause HEAD consistency issues? (Action: infra/storage team)
- Should we add a server-side checksum manifest check during model load that fails fast before attempting to download all shards?

Quick reproducer (for SRE people):
- Simulate network drop: tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem loss 50% delay 200ms
- Run: python tools/repro_load.py --checkpoint s3://staging/llama-test/checkpoint-000 --verbose
- Undo qdisc after test: tc qdisc del dev eth0 root

Notes to self / misc:
- Ticket: INF-721 created for tracking, linked to customer support case CS-8943.
- I uploaded a sanitized log bundle to the diagnosis folder: gs://redwood-diagnosis/INF-721/sofia-logs-20250214.tar.gz
- Ping @Aisha for re-upload of checkpoint-000 (she has access to uploads bucket)

End of scratchpad. Will convert to a clean postmortem if root cause confirmed.
